lines.text: What makes the night sky in the Arctic glow with dancing green and purple ribbons of light?
You are looking at a cosmic battle between the Sun and Earth's magnetic shield.
The Sun constantly ejects a blistering stream of charged solar plasma called the solar wind.
When this solar wind hits Earth, our planet's magnetic field funnels the charged particles toward the magnetic poles.
These energetic particles slam into atmospheric oxygen and nitrogen atoms seventy miles above ground.
The atoms get excited and release excess energy as breathtaking photons: oxygen glows emerald green, while nitrogen shines royal violet.
The auroras are proof that Earth's magnetic force field is keeping us safe from solar storms.
